Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# F1 contract: QEMU plugin exits with code 200 on drain (matches vsim's
3	# kExitHandoffToQemu). 0 is reserved for "workload completed normally".
4	# The orchestrator (F2+) uses this distinction to decide the next spawn.
5	#
6	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
7	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
8	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
9	#   VSIM_ELF     a CSR-trigger fixture (default: handoff_roundtrip.elf)
10	
11	set -euo pipefail
12	
13	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
14	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
15	
16	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
17	hybrid_resolve_paths
18	
19	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
20	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-drain-shared.XXXXXX)
21	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
22	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
23	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
24	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
25	
26	set +e
27	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
28	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
29	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
30	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
31	  -nographic \
32	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
33	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
34	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
35	RC=$?
36	set -e
37	
38	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
39	  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_exit_code]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
40	  echo "--- qemu log ---"
41	  cat "$QEMU_LOG"
42	  exit 1
43	fi
44	
45	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
46	  echo "FAIL[plugin_drain_exit_code]: state file is empty"
47	  exit 1
48	fi
49	
50	echo "[plugin_drain_exit_code] PASS: QEMU exit=$RC, state size=$(wc -c <"$STATE_QEMU") bytes"
51

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# v5 contract: the QEMU plugin drains the L2C MMIO register window into
3	# hybrid_state_v1. The l2c_drain fixture writes 0xA5 to the L2C Control Register
4	# (0xE0500008) and then hits the ROI entry marker; the plugin must set
5	# HYBRID_FLAG_L2C and capture 0xA5 at hybrid_l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL/8].
6	#
7	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
8	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
9	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
10	#   VSIM_ELF     the l2c_drain fixture (FIXTURE=l2c_drain)
11	
12	set -euo pipefail
13	
14	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
16	
17	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-l2c_drain}"
18	hybrid_resolve_paths
19	
20	REPO_ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
21	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
22	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-plugin-l2c-shared.XXXXXX)
23	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
24	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
25	CHECK_SRC=$(mktemp --suffix=.c)
26	CHECK_BIN=$(mktemp)
27	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG" "$CHECK_SRC" "$CHECK_BIN"' EXIT
28	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
29	
30	set +e
31	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
32	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
33	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
34	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
35	  -nographic \
36	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
37	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
38	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
39	RC=$?
40	set -e
41	
42	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
43	  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_drain]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
44	  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"
45	  exit 1
46	fi
47	
48	# Inspect the drained struct via a tiny C checker that shares the ABI header,
49	# so the field offset stays robust to layout changes.
50	cat > "$CHECK_SRC" <<'EOF'
51	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
52	#include <stdio.h>
53	#include <stdlib.h>
54	int main(int argc, char **argv) {
55	    FILE *f = fopen(argv[1], "rb");
56	    if (!f) { fprintf(stderr, "open %s failed\n", argv[1]); return 2; }
57	    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
58	    size_t n = fread(&s, 1, sizeof(s), f);
59	    fclose(f);
60	    if (n != sizeof(s)) { fprintf(stderr, "short read %zu != %zu\n", n, sizeof(s)); return 3; }
61	    if (s.magic != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC) { fprintf(stderr, "bad magic\n"); return 4; }
62	    if (!(s.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_L2C)) { fprintf(stderr, "HYBRID_FLAG_L2C not set\n"); return 5; }
63	    unsigned long long ctrl = (unsigned long long) s.l2c.reg[HYBRID_L2C_OFF_CONTROL / 8];
64	    unsigned long long want = strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 0);
65	    if (ctrl != want) { fprintf(stderr, "l2c ctrl=0x%llx want=0x%llx\n", ctrl, want); return 6; }
66	    printf("OK: HYBRID_FLAG_L2C set, l2c.ctrl=0x%llx\n", ctrl);
67	    return 0;
68	}
69	EOF
70	cc -std=c11 -I "$REPO_ROOT/include" "$CHECK_SRC" -o "$CHECK_BIN"
71	
72	if "$CHECK_BIN" "$STATE_QEMU" 0xA5; then
73	  echo "PASS[plugin_l2c_drain]"
74	else
75	  echo "FAIL[plugin_l2c_drain]: L2C register window not drained correctly"
76	  exit 1
77	fi
78

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# v6 contract: the QEMU plugin tracks which mask-governed CSRs the guest WROTE
3	# and drains that as write_mask[] under HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK. The wm_drain
4	# fixture writes mxstatus + mcache_ctl (read-modify-write-same), and only READS
5	# mmisc_ctl, so:
6	#   - HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK set
7	#   - mxstatus + mcache_ctl bits SET
8	#   - mmisc_ctl bit CLEAR (a csrr must not count as a write)
9	#   - ucode bit SET unconditionally (DSP ops update it without a CSR insn)
10	#
11	# Required environment (auto-detected):
12	#   VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF (FIXTURE=wm_drain)

4	# lm_drain fixture writes known patterns into the hart-0 LM slave ports (ILM
5	# 0xA0000000, DLM 0xA0200000) and the HVM aperture (0x90000000) at the first
6	# and last word of each drained span; the plugin, given the *_size= args,

8	# carrying those patterns. A run WITHOUT the size args (the no-LM/HVM-engine
9	# default) must produce NO sidecar files. QEMU's default HVM is 1 byte
10	# (hvm_size_pow_2=0), so both runs sync the geometry via -global -- the raw
11	# analog of the driver's -readconfig path, which already carries it.
12	#
13	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
14	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
15	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
16	#   VSIM_ELF     the lm_drain fixture (FIXTURE=lm_drain)
17	
18	set -euo pipefail
19	
20	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

22	
23	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-lm_drain}"

34	run_qemu() {  # $1 = extra plugin args appended after outfile ("" for none)
35	  set +e
36	  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
37	    -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
38	    -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \

41	    -nographic \
42	    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \

49	check_word() {  # $1 file, $2 byte offset, $3 expected LE word (8 hex digits)

62	  echo "--- qemu log ---"; cat "$QEMU_LOG"

78	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" 0     444c4d30   # "DLM0" at window start
79	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.dlm" 32764 444c4d31   # "DLM1" at last drained word
80	check_word "$STATE_QEMU.hvm" 0      48564d30  # "HVM0" at window start

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# PC-trigger contract: the drained resume PC equals the --pc-start boundary.
3	#
4	# The drain callback fires BEFORE the trigger insn executes, so the captured
5	# state is pre-execution. A marker is an architectural NOP and may be skipped
6	# (resume at vaddr+size), but a pc boundary is real user code: if the plugin
7	# reports vaddr+size, the boundary insn executes on NEITHER leg (e.g. a
8	# skipped vsetivli leaves vtype.vill set and the vsim window faults on the
9	# first vector op). The plugin must report the boundary's own vaddr so the
10	# insn runs inside the measured window.
11	#
12	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
13	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
14	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
15	#   VSIM_ELF     any fixture with a `main` symbol (default: vplat_hello.elf)
16	
17	set -uo pipefail
18	
19	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
20	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
21	
22	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-vplat_hello}"
23	hybrid_resolve_paths
24	
25	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
26	command -v "${NM:-nm}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || NM=nm
27	ENTER_HEX=$("$NM" "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '$3 == "main" { print $1; exit }')
28	[ -n "$ENTER_HEX" ] || { echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: no main in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
29	ENTER=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$ENTER_HEX")
30	
31	SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
32	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-pcresume-shared.XXXXXX)
33	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
34	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
35	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
36	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
37	
38	set +e
39	"$VSIM_QEMU" \
40	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
41	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
42	  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
43	  -nographic \
44	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
45	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
46	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU,enter_pc=$ENTER" \
47	  </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
48	RC=$?
49	set -e
50	
51	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
52	  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
53	  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
54	  exit 1
55	fi
56	if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$ENTER)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
57	  echo "FAIL[pc_trigger_resume_pc]: resume PC != pc-start boundary $ENTER:"
58	  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
59	  exit 1
60	fi
61	echo "[pc_trigger_resume_pc] PASS: drain resumes at the boundary insn ($ENTER)"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Oracle exit-drain contract (verify_oracle F1): a pure-QEMU run drains
3	# hybrid_state_v1 at the ROI EXIT boundary, producing the reference state the
4	# differential verifier compares against the vsim drain.
5	#
6	# Semantics: arm on the exit boundary's exec callback, drain on the NEXT exec
7	# callback. That callback fires before its own insn executes, so the captured
8	# state is "after the boundary insn retired" -- exactly what vsim's exit drain
9	# records (DPC = next insn to execute) -- and the reported pc is the next
10	# insn's vaddr, correct even for a branching boundary insn.
11	#
12	# Cases:
13	#   1. exit_marker=1  -- arm on `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1`; pc must be marker+4
14	#                        (NOT enter-marker+4: the ENTER marker must not drain).
15	#   2. exit_pc=0x...  -- arm on the boundary vaddr; same expectation when the
16	#                        boundary is the (fall-through) exit marker.
17	#   3. drain_pc=0x... -- sample at a later, caller-chosen pc instead of the
18	#                        very next insn. The differential harness passes
19	#                        vsim's actual halt pc here: vsim's DMI halt lands a
20	#                        variable 0-3 insns past the trigger, and both sides
21	#                        must sample the SAME architectural point.
22	#   4. drain_pc=0x... alone -- install error: drain_pc requires an oracle
23	#                        anchor (exit_marker / exit_pc).
24	#
25	# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
26	#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
27	#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
28	#   FIXTURE      a marker-carrying fixture (default: rt_c_hello)
29	
30	set -uo pipefail
31	
32	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
33	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
34	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/roi.sh"
35	
36	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_hello}"
37	hybrid_resolve_paths
38	
39	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
40	OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
41	command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "skip[oracle_exit_drain]: no objdump"; exit 77; }
42	
43	MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")") \
44	  || { echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: no ROI markers in $VSIM_ELF"; exit 1; }
45	EXIT_PC="0x${MARKERS##* }"
46	# The exit marker is a 4-byte NOP that falls through, so the first insn
47	# executed after it retires sits at marker+4.
48	WANT_PC=$(printf '0x%x' $((EXIT_PC + 4)))
49	
50	STATE=$(mktemp)
51	QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
52	trap 'rm -f "$STATE" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT
53	
54	run_qemu() {  # $1 = plugin arg suffix (script runs without -e; RC checked per case)
55	  "$VSIM_QEMU" \
56	    -machine andes_ae350 \
57	    -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
58	    -nographic \
59	    -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
60	    -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
61	    -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE,$1" \
62	    </dev/null >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
63	  RC=$?
64	}
65	
66	check_drain() {  # $1 = case label
67	  if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
68	    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: expected QEMU exit=200 on drain, got $RC"
69	    tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
70	    exit 1
71	  fi
72	  if [ ! -s "$STATE" ]; then
73	    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: no state file written"
74	    exit 1
75	  fi
76	  if ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$WANT_PC)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
77	    echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: $1: drain pc != exit-marker+4 ($WANT_PC):"
78	    grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
79	    exit 1
80	  fi
81	}
82	
83	# Case 1: marker mode.
84	run_qemu "exit_marker=1"
85	check_drain "exit_marker"
86	
87	# Case 2: pc mode, boundary = the exit marker's own vaddr.
88	: > "$STATE"
89	run_qemu "exit_pc=$EXIT_PC"
90	check_drain "exit_pc"
91	
92	# Case 3: drain_pc skips past intermediate ticks and samples the chosen pc.
93	# Use the third insn after the exit marker (straight-line in rt_c_hello's
94	# epilogue), derived from the disassembly so insn sizes don't matter.
95	DRAIN_PC=0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF" | awk '
96	  /5a102013/ { n = NR }
97	  n && NR == n + 3 { sub(/:$/, "", $1); print $1; exit }')
98	: > "$STATE"
99	run_qemu "exit_marker=1,drain_pc=$DRAIN_PC"
100	if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ] || ! grep -q "drained state to .* (pc=$DRAIN_PC)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
101	  echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: drain_pc: expected drain at $DRAIN_PC (rc=$RC):"
102	  grep "drained state" "$QEMU_LOG" || tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
103	  exit 1
104	fi
105	
106	# Case 4: drain_pc needs an oracle anchor (exit_marker / exit_pc).
107	run_qemu "drain_pc=$DRAIN_PC"
108	if [ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || ! grep -qi "drain_pc.*requires" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
109	  echo "FAIL[oracle_exit_drain]: bare drain_pc should fail install (got rc=$RC):"
110	  tail -5 "$QEMU_LOG"
111	  exit 1
112	fi
113	
114	echo "[oracle_exit_drain] PASS: oracle drains after the ROI exit boundary (pc=$WANT_PC)"

1	# Shared path resolution for the top-level e2e harness + drivers.
2	# Sourced (not executed). Provides:
3	#   TOP_ROOT                  - absolute path of the repo root
4	#   hybrid_resolve_paths()    - sets VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN,
5	#                               VSIM_ELF from TOP_ROOT (unless already
6	#                               exported by caller) and exits 77 (CTest
7	#                               skip) if any artifact is missing. Reads
8	#                               FIXTURE for the VSIM_ELF default.
9	#   hybrid_describe_int F [BIN] - print integer field F from an engine's
10	#                               --describe JSON (BIN defaults to $VSIM_BIN);
11	#                               empty output if absent/unprobeable. The ONE
12	#                               shell parser of the descriptor wire format.
13	
14	TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
15	TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)
16	
17	if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then
18	  . "$TOP_ROOT/config.env"
19	fi
20	
21	hybrid_resolve_paths() {
22	  # VSIM_BIN_DIR / QEMU_BIN_DIR come from the environment or from the
23	  # config.env sourced above; there is no in-tree fallback (both simulators
24	  # are external prebuilts). Unset -> a nonexistent path -> skip below.
25	  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-${VSIM_BIN_DIR:-}/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"
26	  VSIM_QEMU="${VSIM_QEMU:-${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-}/qemu-system-riscv64}"
27	  VSIM_PLUGIN="${VSIM_PLUGIN:-$TOP_ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so}"
28	  VSIM_ELF="${VSIM_ELF:-$TOP_ROOT/tests/fixtures/${FIXTURE}.elf}"
29	  for f in "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_QEMU" "$VSIM_PLUGIN" "$VSIM_ELF"; do
30	    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
31	      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
32	      exit 77
33	    fi
34	  done
35	}
36	
37	# Extract one integer field from an engine's --describe JSON. $1 = field name,
38	# $2 = engine binary (default $VSIM_BIN). Prints nothing when the field is
39	# absent or the binary cannot be probed, so callers can `[ -n ... ]`-gate.
40	hybrid_describe_int() {
41	  "${2:-$VSIM_BIN}" --describe 2>/dev/null \
42	    | sed -n "s/.*\"$1\": *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p" | head -n1
43	}
44	
45	# Write a 32-bit little-endian word into a binary file (pattern staging for
46	# the LM/HVM backdoor-load tests). $1 = file, $2 = byte offset, $3 = value.
47	put_word_le() {
48	  local v=$3 bytes="" i
49	  for i in 0 8 16 24; do
50	    bytes+=$(printf '\\x%02x' $(( (v >> i) & 0xff )))
51	  done
52	  # shellcheck disable=SC2059
53	  printf "$bytes" | dd of="$1" bs=1 seek="$2" conv=notrunc status=none
54	}
